internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rates in Checkout Service
internal.body:
At 11:08 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered due to a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified error injection as the primary fault type causing failures in the checkout service, supported by a high error ratio of 0.475. Concurrently, the payment service also exhibited a high error ratio of 0.5, reinforcing the error injection hypothesis.

Multiple remediation proposals were generated but initially blocked by guardrails due to target mismatches and missing dry run validations. Despite these challenges, the diagnosis consistently pointed to error injection in the checkout service as the root cause.

The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution. No recovery actions were successfully verified during this incident window.

Key timeline events:
- 11:08:56: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 11:28:48: Diagnosis round 1 confirmed error injection in checkout
- 11:28:54 to 11:29:16: Multiple proposals refused by guardrails
- Incident escalated for further handling

Severity: SEV2

external.title: Some checkouts failed
external.body: Between 11:08 and 11:30 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to elevated error rates in the checkout service. Our team identified the cause as an internal error injection affecting service reliability. We escalated the issue for further investigation and are working to resolve it. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.
